label: <DEL> step in longer sequences (plus late original / first copy steps)
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: the <DEL> step holds 66% of activation mass, fires on 37.5% of <DEL> steps, and all of the strongest activations are at <DEL>. The firing rate rises with sequence length (L=3-5 rarely; L=9 most). Smaller weaker components: the last few original tokens of long sequences (t>=6, ~22% of mass) and the first one or two copy steps (recall_idx 1-2, ~12%). Never active at t=0-1 and almost never deep in the copy phase. Activation is weakly higher when the sequence contains d, f, c, x, 3, r, but adding that only slightly improves F1 (0.53 to 0.56), so it is left out. Even in long sequences many <DEL> steps stay inactive, so precision is about 0.5 and the predicate does not cover the non-delimiter mass.
